_comment_functionTimeout: For the nightly reconcileEagle timer: a full run measured ~5 minutes against test, and Flex Consumption defaults functionTimeout to 30 minutes, so the timers keep their ceiling. The HTTP routes are unaffected — the platform caps a request at ~230 s regardless of this.

applicationInsights._comment: enablePerformanceCountersCollection is the HOST-side half of the perf counter cut. api/index.js turned off the Node worker distro's counters (SDKVersion flm_node22:...:dst1.19.0); this turns off the Functions host's Kudu counters (SDKVersion af_azwapccore:2.23.0-29), which kept flowing afterwards because they come from a different process. Measured over the 26h before the worker-side change: distro 10822 records / 5.23 MB, host 4623 / 3.55 MB, so neither half is negligible. Everything both emitted - % Processor Time, Private Bytes, Available Bytes - is already collected as App Service platform metrics at no charge and outside this workspace's dailyQuotaGb. Note APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_ENABLE_AGENT=false in api-function-flex.bicep does NOT cover this; the platform agent and the host's own AI integration are separate, which is why the counters survived that setting being false all along.

samplingSettings._comment: DO NOT add Exception or Trace here to protect application logs - it does not do that. This section configures the ApplicationInsights provider inside the Functions HOST process. The app's winston output never takes that path: api/index.js starts the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distro inside the Node WORKER, which exports log records through its own exporter at samplingRatio 1.0, i.e. already unsampled. The worker-side knob is useAzureMonitor({ samplingRatio }), not this. Excluding Trace here only stops the host's own per-request lines being sampled, which removes the one backpressure valve on the telemetry class that scales with traffic - and hitting dailyQuotaGb stops collection entirely, which is strictly worse than sampling it.

queues._comment: messageEncoding 'none' because the bulk-download producer sends a bare job UUID as the message body: the default base64 encoding would have the trigger hand the worker a decoded-then-re-decoded string that is not the id. batchSize 1 with newBatchThreshold 0 is one zip per instance — Flex scales horizontally to 20 instances, and one 64 MiB multipart buffer per 2048 MB instance is the memory budget this keeps. The 64 MiB is real only because src/storage/minio.js constructs the client with partSize 64 MiB: with no size hint the SDK picks the part size that fits a 5 TB object in 10,000 parts, 528 MiB, and buffers each one. maxDequeueCount is read by api/index.js, which tells the worker which delivery is the last. visibilityTimeout matches the 30-minute functionTimeout with room to spare, so a message from an instance killed mid-zip reappears rather than being lost.
